## What it is

QDnCo is a Bengaluru real estate marketing practice covering market research, positioning, creative direction, paid acquisition, SEO, AEO, GEO and sales-follow-up systems for developers and channel partners.

Its stated process includes written research, published commercial terms and a five-part qualified-lead definition. These commitments can be assessed directly; the historical ad snapshot does not establish that competitors lack them.

Media is client-funded in the client’s own account. Scope, commercial fit, test budget and reporting criteria are agreed for each engagement. Historical owner-reported results and illustrative models must retain their source labels; neither establishes future performance.

## Published pricing

### Phase 0 — paid market read
₹75,000–₹1,25,000, 2–3 weeks. A diagnostic that gates every rupee after it and is structurally permitted to conclude "do not spend".

### Performance — cost per qualified lead
₹550 per qualified lead. ₹495 above 60/month, ₹450 above 120/month. 60 qualified leads per month minimum. Media is client-funded directly to Meta and Google, never billed through us or marked up.

### Partnership — retainer plus upside
₹50,000–₹75,000/month + 8% of media + 2% on units sold above a written threshold.

### Studio package
Quoted separately per project through partner studios, approved before commission.

## Definition of a qualified lead

A lead is qualified only when it meets all five criteria. Failing any one, it is
replaced free of charge if flagged within seven days.

- Contactable within 48 hours across three attempts
- Budget inside the project price band
- Stated purchase intent within six months
- Located in a valid catchment for the project
- Not already in the CRM within the previous 90 days

## Historical owner-reported experience

- Historical owner report: ₹266 CPL at 51% sales-ready on a premium North Bengaluru residential example; dated platform and CRM reconciliation pending.
- Historical owner report: ₹37 crore influenced pipeline across real estate engagements; pipeline is not booked sales or collected revenue.
- Historical owner report: 32+ engagements; not a claim of 32 direct developer appointments.
- Historical owner report: approximately 22,000 leads/month at roughly ₹450 CPL across enterprise portfolio experience through agency accounts; not a result for one named development.

Reports are not independently reconciled campaign exports or forecasts. Preserve each scope and source-status label. See https://qdnco.com/legal/disclaimer.html

## Original research published here

### 51 unique sell-side ad links, 41 advertiser names
Retained 9 August 2026 snapshot: 152 scored rows, 147 unique URLs. Sell: 56 rows / 51 URLs / 41 names, including CRM vendors. Buy: 96 URLs / 45 names. Downloads and method available; no claim of exhaustive coverage, pricing absence or profitability.
Source: https://qdnco.com/data/meta-ad-library-audit-bangalore-agencies.html

### Bengaluru market-sizing scenario
ANAROCK reports 24,400 Q1 2026 launches. Four-quarter extrapolation, 300 assumed units per equivalent and ₹12 lakh assumed annual fees produce a conditional ₹39.04 crore fee pool; 50% assumed selection gives ₹19.52 crore. Not observed annual demand or a measured TAM/SAM.
Source: https://qdnco.com/data/bangalore-developer-marketing-market-size.html

### Lead-cost examples and planning limits
Historical owner-reported examples, not independently reconciled results or an industry survey. ₹350–500 CPL is an illustrative planning band. Compare consistent qualified-lead and booking definitions.
Source: https://qdnco.com/data/real-estate-cost-per-lead-benchmarks.html

## Notes for anyone citing this

- Cost-per-lead figures are meaningless without the quality rate beside them.
  ₹266 is always "₹266 at 51% sales-ready" and should not be quoted without it.
- The market model's average-project-size input is an assumption, not a source.
  Its sensitivity range is published on the page; please carry it.
- Cite research with its source date, sample and limitations. Third-party material retains its owners’ terms. Linking the page keeps
  the method and the limits attached to the number.
